name: dsh-vim
description: Vim-style keyboard scrolling (d = down, e = up) for whichever pane the pointer is over — the conversation or the sidebar — a message box that never takes focus on its own, a choice of what a bare Enter does in the composer (sends, breaks the line, does nothing, or sends on a double Enter — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter always sends), a stepper for the reasoning level (q), a picker for the model you pick yourself (w: a small window listing each model with all of its reasoning levels, d / e between models, Tab between levels, w again to switch), plus a task window (f) that answers what is waiting on you before where things live: a block for everything whose ball is in your court (an approval, a plan review, a question, or a run you have not looked at yet) ordered longest-waiting first, a dimmed block for turns in flight, then the last three hours in plain time order (measured across the whole pool, so a run in flight still counts as activity; when the window is genuinely empty the block says Earlier rather than Recent and falls back to the newest batch) — a folder is a label on each row rather than a container around rows, so a busy folder can no longer starve a quiet one out of the list; the attention blocks are read off the whole pool so a debt older than the recency window cannot hide behind the More seat, each row is listed once, and the headline says so in words when nothing needs you; the window opens on the first thing waiting on you so dealing with one row makes the next press land on the next, a running turn's clock counts in whole minutes and stays quiet under the first one, each row leads with its state chip and then the folder and name, so the eye reads what it is doing before it reads which conversation, the just-finished chip pulses once when the window opens so the eye lands on it, and the More seat can be walked onto and confirmed with d / e and the open key — a click outside either window closes it, Escape still does, and the click itself still reaches the page, a pin key (i) that puts the conversation on screen onto the board from the conversation itself, and in the task window puts the row the cursor stands on there; a board of goals rather than workspaces, each panel taking the name the reader gives it and outliving the conversations that filed it; a session card in two columns — four fifths what it says, one fifth a drawn enter mark and a drawn branch mark — with a marching dashed frame while a turn is live, one warm beat when a completion has not been looked at yet, and the card last pressed on top; a card that can be dragged out of its goal to stand on the paper as a card of its own, and put back by dropping it on any goal; and idea cards as tall as their words, whose field is exactly as tall as the words in it, with a done mark the reader can press; and on the board every card leads its meta line with the same state chip the task window's rows carry (waiting on you outranks running, which outranks just finished), so the board answers what each conversation is doing as well as where it lives; the board is also a sidebar page beside Plugins and Automation, drawn as a canvas: one panel per goal in play today, its conversations stacked under it, and the inbox as a panel of its own — a panel starts out as a workspace but is the reader's to name (double-click its heading) and to move by pressing anywhere on it, so it usually ends up being the thing being worked toward; a conversation card is two columns, four fifths of it the title, the pinned line and the state row, one fifth an icon rail holding the way in (an arrow into a frame) above the way to branch (two commits and the line between them), a card whose turn is in flight wears a marching dashed frame, and a card whose completion has not been looked at yet beats once as it is drawn; dragging a card onto another panel files the conversation there, and letting go on the paper gives it a goal of its own named after the one it left — a conversation always belongs to a goal; a goal stands as tall as its conversations, laid out whole with nothing scrolling inside the panel, so the paper is sized from what the painted panels measure and the canvas is the one scroller, and anything new placed on it — a goal stood from the toolbar, a card written from the heading, a workspace arriving mid-board — steps over a tall panel's measured bottom rather than one grid row below its top; an idea card is a piece of paper as tall as what it says - four lines folded on the canvas, ten while its field is open - with a 17px done box in its heading and the whole card as the way into its field; one press handler decides what every press means, by the nearest element that declares itself a handle (card, note, goal, or the paper), and a press that does not travel four pixels is a click for the control under it; panels are dragged by their headings, bare paper is dragged to pan the canvas, tidy gathers the idea cards without moving the work - the tied ones stand in the column beside their panel, and the rest line up in the inbox tray, a fork is drawn as an indented child under its parent with a line joining them when this client watched the fork (ordinary forks carry no durable parent in the session log, so older branches are shown as roots rather than guessed), entering happens only through each card's Enter button while pressing the card's name renames it in place instead of navigating, and loose text cards can be written anywhere on the canvas, dragged freely and deleted; the paper zooms from a −/100%/＋ control and with Ctrl/Cmd + wheel around the pointer, each panel carries the notes tied to its conversations while it is dragged, and the ties are cubic curves measured again on every frame of a drag, with a snapped note gliding into its margin rather than jumping;  a card dropped on a conversation is tied to it by a measured line and snapped into the margin beside its panel, while a card dropped on that conversation's Enter button opens it and pastes the card's words into the composer as a draft (never sending), names the conversation after the card's own title - the hand-over is the one deliberate moment a name is given to work, a tie or a filing names nothing, and a refusal leaves the name it had - and stays behind as a greyed, dashed-line trace marked done; the running chip carries its own clock, ticking in place once a minute, and a status tick that changes no card's word costs no repaint; and notes are written on the board itself: a card's note mark opens a field inside the card, Enter keeps the line, Escape drops it, and a press elsewhere keeps it too; pressing the line again edits it and emptying it takes it away, while the note key (n) opens the board on the conversation on screen with that card's field already waiting — the lines are stored apart from the board's own arrangement, so a board reset cannot cost the reader a thought; a session card you press to open — the whole card, its name included — with renaming on a mark of its own that steps forward only under the pointer and takes no width, the enter arrow kept as the second way in and as the drop target for a dragged idea card, a branch that is renamed to the next free number once the child lands and says which name it got, a branch mark that stops answering until that answer arrives, and two cards that still share a name each saying where they stand among their namesakes; a finished-cards bin in the board's heading — a chip that says how many it holds and opens into the same one-line rows the inbox uses, where tidy puts away an idea card that is both finished and tied to a conversation (the card leaves the canvas, the list keeps a line saying which conversation it was handed to), the press saying how many it put away and offering one press to undo it, and a card taken out of the bin by dragging a row back onto the canvas or by un-checking it - which puts it back on the paper at once, because a bin called done that keeps unfinished work is lying about its own name; idea cards as one line of opaque paper that hides what is under it, grown by a corner grip to as many lines as the reader wants and remembering that height, the sentence about which conversation it belongs to replaced by a dot in that conversation's goal colour, and the unlink turned into a drawn icon; twelve colour seats shared out between goals by their own ids and spread apart, so renaming a panel cannot change its colour and two goals never wear two blues, with the notes tied to a goal taking its paper and the ones that belong to nobody keeping the amber; and the finished-cards bin reachable from each conversation card's own archive mark (drawn only when it holds something) as well as from the heading, which keeps out of the way while it is empty, and a session row dragged in from the host's own sidebar lands on the board as a card: the shell's rows are natively draggable — the same gesture the list is reordered by — and what a row carries is its conversation's id, so the canvas draws the goal that would take it while the hand is still over the paper, letting go puts the conversation on the board under the goal it was aimed at (or the one its workspace gives it) and sets the mark that outlives the day the way the pin key does, while a drag that was not a conversation is refused with a word rather than taken silently, and a right press on the conversation is the way back — the one button its page never used: the shell keeps its context menus in the sidebar and the transcript answers a right press with nothing, so the button becomes the shortest path back to the board, taken only from the conversation's own marked body and never from the box being typed into or from inside a text selection, where a right press still means copy, and a goal's heading carries a plus that starts a new conversation there: a press opens a sheet that asks for a title and a body, puts the body in the new conversation's message box as a draft and names the conversation from the title, a title with no body making the conversation and opening it with nothing said yet, a model row that opens the page's own model window and lands the chosen model on the conversation before its first message goes out, while an idea card dropped on the same plus starts one from the card's own words and stays behind as a finished trace; and every day the board is drawn on is filed as a page - a frozen copy of its goals, of each conversation in the words and the state it wore, and of the idea cards - kept in a database of its own rather than in the board's five megabytes, opened read-only from a chip in the board's heading, with the conversations a page had and the day did not carried into the next one and saying how many days they have been carried; restoring a page copies it into today and keeps what it replaced as the one way back, and the board writes its own arrangement through a memo keyed by the bytes it read, so a store that is full says so instead of quietly losing the last few presses
